title: My Health Insurance Readiness Checklist
description: A personal readiness assessment helping students evaluate their health insurance literacy across five critical areas—from understanding coverage basics to knowing where to find individual coverage when needed.
instructions: For each category below, rate your current knowledge level. For any items where you select 'Need to learn more,' write one specific action you'll take to address that gap.

categories.title: Coverage Timeline
categories.question: I know when I will age off my parent's plan (or if I already have my own coverage, I know my renewal date)
categories.action_prompt: What specific step will you take to find out your coverage end date or renewal date?

categories.title: Cost Vocabulary
categories.question: I can define premium, deductible, copay, coinsurance, and out-of-pocket maximum in my own words
categories.action_prompt: What resource will you use to review and memorize these five key terms?

categories.title: Where to Find Coverage
categories.question: I know where I would go to find individual health coverage if I needed it today (healthcare.gov, employer HR, Medicaid office)
categories.action_prompt: What is one specific website or phone number you'll bookmark/save for finding coverage?

categories.title: Special Enrollment
categories.question: I know what triggers a Special Enrollment Period and how long the window lasts
categories.action_prompt: What life event are you most likely to experience in the next 5 years, and what will you need to do when it happens?

categories.title: Plan Comparison
categories.question: I can calculate roughly how much a $2,000 medical bill would cost me under two different plan types
categories.action_prompt: What is one practice problem you'll work through to build your cost-calculation skills?

ready.message: You're well-prepared to navigate health insurance decisions. Keep this knowledge fresh and revisit it when you turn 26 or start a new job.

developing.message: You have a solid foundation, but there are a few gaps to address. Focus on the action steps you identified for 'Need to learn more' items.

beginning.message: You have important learning ahead. Prioritize your action steps and revisit this chapter's key concepts. Health insurance literacy is not optional.

completion_message: Your Health Insurance Readiness Checklist has been saved to your portfolio. Come back to it when you turn 26, start a new job, or have a major life change. The action steps you wrote today will guide you when the time comes.
